title: fix(lint): a list view written into a package and bound outside its closure is reported at the save door, not skipped
body:
Fixes #24563

Clause-②: yes

At the runtime save door, a list view written into a package is now judged against that package's closure (ruling #9612: the package, its declared dependencies, platform/system objects, and provenance-less overlay rows) instead of being skipped:

- **A binding outside the closure is reported, never skipped.** This covers an object of a package the writing package never declared, and an object that exists nowhere. It gets one `list-view-object-outside-closure` finding at `warning`, located at the key the binding is read from (`views[0].data.object`). The hint names the remedy: declare a dependency on the package that defines the object in the `dependencies` of the writing package's manifest. That is the verdict a flow's out-of-closure trigger object gets at the same door (P2), so the write is still stored and the finding rides the 2xx `advisories`.
- **A binding inside the closure keeps its field verdict.** An unknown `columns` field is refused `422 list-view-field-unknown`, as the overlay door refuses it (unchanged, now pinned at both layers).
- A write that names no package, and the CLI commands, are unchanged.

## Read first: the declaration differs from the claim

The claim (`6271302258`) and the dispatch carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. That line was written when the out-of-closure binding was expected to be refused. P2 measured a flow's out-of-closure object reference at advisory severity. The dispatch's own prohibition says that in that case "the view gets the same advisory for the binding, and the in-closure field refusal stays as it is". So this PR refuses nothing that was accepted before: no accept set narrows. The public surface does grow, by an optional `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope`, an optional second argument to `validateListViewFieldRefs`, and two new exports (`LIST_VIEW_OBJECT_OUTSIDE_CLOSURE`, `ListViewFieldRefOptions`). That is `Clause-②: yes` by the definition "does this card widen the accept set or enlarge the public surface". So this body and the changeset declare `Clause-②: yes` at `minor`, with no `!`, no FROM / TO lines and no ADR-0087 disposition. The claim's line is the seat's to correct, or this body's if the seat rules otherwise.

## What changes

- **`packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`.** Skip 1 (`:818`) splits in two:
  - when the caller states a package closure (`ListViewFieldRefOptions.packageScope`), a binding missing from `stack.objects` is reported once per list view, at the key it was read from (`data.object`, else the container's `objectName` / `object`, else the object's `name`). The positions are not judged against anything else;
  - with no closure stated, the skip is unchanged. Skip 2 (an object that is present but has no readable field map) is unchanged under a closure too.

  An empty graph under a closure is still judged, because every binding is then outside it. The module header gains the section that explains this, and its "does NOT own" note names the one exception.
- **`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`.** `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` puts `packageScope` on the rule context exactly when it narrowed the snapshots. One predicate, `packageScopeInForce`, now decides both that and `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`'s early return. The four limbs are untouched. The guard's behaviour is byte-identical, and the existing "narrows NOTHING when no scope / an empty package id" pins hold it.
- **`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`** (interface only): `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope?`, documented as set only by the runtime gate and read only by this rule.
- **`packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`.** `ReferenceIntegrityRunOptions.packageScope?`. The `validateListViewFieldRefs` member hands the scope to the rule. Its `runtimeTypes` are unchanged (`['flow', 'view', 'object']`). `validateObjectReferences` is unchanged (`['flow', 'dataset']`, `:224`).
- **`packages/lint/src/index.ts`.** Exports the new rule id and options type (`rule-id-barrel-exports.test.ts` requires the id).
- **Pins.**
  - Lint level: a block in `runtime-gate.package-closure.test.ts`, through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, covering:
    - out-of-closure binding reported, `nosuch_obj` reported, and reported under an empty closure;
    - in-closure unknown field refused, in-closure known field admitted;
    - declared dependency admitted (known field) and refused (unknown field);
    - system object by prefix and by `isSystem`, and a provenance-less overlay object, each keeping its field verdict;
    - the no-package write unchanged (the stranger column still refused, `nosuch_obj` still silent, an empty package id narrows nothing);
    - the flow verdict unchanged, with a stored sibling's out-of-closure list view cancelling in the differential and reported when that object is itself written;
    - the CLI reading unchanged.
  - Protocol level: the engine-lane rider declared on #6367 (`6271671580`). It is a block in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, through the real `saveMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`, over a registry with three packages and a platform object:
    - (a) the active save is reported, for the stranger's object and for `nosuch_obj`;
    - (b) in-closure unknown `columns` field refused `422` at `views[0].columns[1].field` and nothing stored, and the known field saves clean, for own, declared-dependency and platform objects;
    - (c) the overlay door is unchanged;
    - (d) draft promotion: reported, and the in-closure case refused;
    - (e) package draft publish: reported on `published[].advisories`, and the in-closure case refused;
    - (f) a view bound to an object drafted in the same batch: no phantom report, and its fields judged.

    Test file only. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is untouched (PR #24599).
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/24563-list-view-out-of-closure.md`, `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes`.
- **Docs:** one sentence in `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` (see "File surface beyond the claim").

## Premises (measured on this branch)

**P1. Holds.** The probe was the real `saveMetaItem` / `publishPackageDrafts` over the `protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts` stub-engine shape: a registry holding `com.acme.crm` (declares `com.acme.core`), `com.acme.core`, a stranger `com.other.analytics`, and a platform object. The body is the card's, a flattened list overlay with `columns: [title, zzz_nope]`. It ran before and after through the same probe; the HTTP door was not booted.

- Before (`origin/main` `5a871e4e41`, lint built from it):
  - written into `com.acme.crm`, bound to the stranger's object: `RESOLVED success=true state=active advisories=[]`;
  - bound to `nosuch_obj`: `RESOLVED success=true state=active advisories=[]`;
  - overlay (no package), stranger's object: `REFUSED 422 INVALID_METADATA issues=[["list-view-field-unknown","error","views[0].columns[1].field"]]`;
  - draft → `publishPackageDrafts`: `outcome=published published=1 failed=[] probes={"issues":[],...}`.
  - The in-closure controls (own, declared dependency, platform) were already refused `422 list-view-field-unknown`.
- After (this branch):
  - stranger's object: `RESOLVED success=true state=active advisories=[["list-view-object-outside-closure","warning","views[0].data.object"]]`;
  - `nosuch_obj`: the same advisory;
  - overlay: unchanged (`422`, and `nosuch_obj` there `200` with `advisories=[]`);
  - `publishPackageDrafts`: `published=1` with `published[0].advisories=[["list-view-object-outside-closure","warning","views[0].data.object"]]`;
  - in-closure controls: unchanged.
- The protocol block run against the ablated rule (the skip restored, below) is the same "before" through the pinned door: 4 red with `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'list-view-object-outside-closure' ]`.

**P2. Holds: advisory.**

- Rule `validateFlowTriggerReadiness`, issue code `flow-trigger-unknown-object`, severity `warning`.
- Produced at `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:446-449`, the record-trigger branch: `objectName && !objectNames.has(objectName) && !objectName.startsWith('sys_')` with `severity: 'warning'`. The `timeRelative` twin is at `:498-501`.
- It reaches the door through `authoring-rules.ts:1365` (`surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`).
- Pinned at the lint level at `runtime-gate.package-closure.test.ts:246` ("Measured severity here is advisory (`warning`), so it reports rather than refuses"), and at the door at `protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts:211` (`['flow-trigger-unknown-object']`, `success: true`).
- One more reading the seat should see. The **dataset** door does not agree. `validateObjectReferences` runs on `dataset` writes, and under the same closure it REFUSES an out-of-closure base object: `errors=["error:object-reference-unknown@datasets.crm_ds.object"]`, and `[]` for the same body with no package. So the door has two verdicts today for "an object outside the package's closure": flow advisory, dataset refusal. Per the dispatch the view takes the flow's. The question is raised in the report.

**P3. Holds.** No shipped view binds an object outside its package's closure. The door's `view` rule set (`validatePresetComparands`, `validateReferenceIntegrity`, `validateVisibilityPredicates`, `validatePredicatePathRefs`) was run over every shipped view, with its package's scope and without, before and after this change.

- Universe: every package's objects stamped with its owner, plus all 83 platform objects from every `*.object.ts` under `packages/` outside `spec`. All 83 are system objects (`isSystemObject`), so 118 objects in all.
- Packages and their manifest `dependencies`:
  - `examples/app-crm` (composed stack): `com.example.crm`, none, 3 views;
  - `examples/app-todo` (composed stack): `com.example.todo`, none, 1 view;
  - `examples/app-showcase` (the barrels the config imports, because the composed config imports unbuilt connectors): `com.example.showcase`, none, 6 views;
  - `examples/app-multi-package`: `com.example.multi.core` (none) and `com.example.multi.orders` (`com.example.multi.core`), 0 views;
  - the `create-objectstack` blank template (its barrels): 0 views;
  - `packages/qa/downstream-contract` (`ContractStack`): `com.objectstack.downstream-contract`, none, 1 view.
- 11 views, 39 list-view bindings: 0 outside the closure, and 0 findings scoped or whole, before and after. Every example object written as an `object` under its package's scope: 0 list-view findings.
- The platform's 97 built-in list views: none retargets `data.object`.
- Control through the same harness: the CRM lead view retargeted at `showcase_task`, under `com.example.crm`, draws 3 advisories (`list` and its two `listViews`) and 0 errors.

## Mechanism assumptions

- **G1. The list-view rule reports the binding itself, scoped by a stated closure.** Adding `'view'` to `validateObjectReferences` was measured and rejected, for three reasons:
  - its ladder answers `error` for an unprefixed unresolved name. Package scope, out-of-closure: `["error:object-reference-unknown@views[0].object"]`. That is a refusal, not the P2 verdict;
  - it reads only the container's own `views[].object`. A body binding through `data.object` alone answered `[]`;
  - it would refuse an overlay write bound to an object that exists nowhere (`["error:object-reference-unknown@views[0].object"]` with no package; today `200`), which changes the overlay door.

  Reporting only under a stated closure keeps the overlay door and the CLI byte-identical. The only channel that tells a rule a closure is in force is the rule context, hence `packageScope`.
- **G2. Held.** Both layers are pinned (above). There was no `protocol.ts` change.
- **G3. Falsified in part, by P2.** The out-of-closure binding is advisory and the in-closure refusal already existed, so no accept set narrows.
  - The changeset is `minor` on the public-surface growth, with `Clause-②: yes`.
  - There is no `!`, no FROM / TO, and no ADR-0087 marker: `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` reads no breaking declaration.
  - The Fix line is there: declare the dependency, or bind inside the closure, after which the field is judged.
- **G4. Main moved** `5a871e4e41` → `c3954057fe` (5 commits, none in `lint` or `metadata-protocol`; `spec` moved). It was merged with `bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`: steps 1–3, with no additional changes. Step 4: the `metadata-protocol` dependency closure was rebuilt, and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` reports all 14 generated artifacts up to date. This branch edits no generated artifact.

## Verification

- Pre-merge head `cab356c0ce` (the same code as `fe5bafb2be`, which added only the changeset and the docs sentence):
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 248 files passed (3 skipped), 20731 tests passed (19 skipped). `typecheck` passed.
- Merge head `8a295d8477`:
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 148 files, 6934 tests passed. `typecheck` (with `check:test-typecheck`) passed.
  - `metadata-protocol`: `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, `protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts` and `protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts` passed 175/175. `typecheck` passed. The merge brought no `metadata-protocol` or `lint` change.
- **Ablation**, after the fix was committed (`fe5bafb2be`):
  - Mutation, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: `if (scope) reportOutsideClosure(...)` became `if (scope && String(object) === 'ablated_24563_no_report') reportOutsideClosure(...)`. Anchor 1 → 0, blob `df4ce7aa8c22` → `7340a202512b`. Lint was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 4 built files.
  - Mutated: in the lint file, 5 red and 22 green. The reds were the three report cases, the object-door assertion in the flow case, and the scoped half of the CLI case. The field-verdict and no-package cases stayed green. The protocol block had 4 red ((a) ×2, (d), (e)) and 4 green ((b) ×2, (c), (f)).
  - Restore leg: blob equal to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuild, then `--absent`: absent from all 20 built files, tree clean. The lint file passed 27/27 and the protocol file 160/160.
- Consumer suites were not rerun. The public surface grows by optional members only, and no consumer passes the new argument.

## Gates

These were run on the merge head `8a295d8477`, which is the PR head.

- **Local, derived.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths, derived 93 families from 9 changed paths against merge base `c3954057f`. Each ran verbatim, with its exit code recorded before any pipe.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: "93 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 92 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)", exit 0.
  - 92 exited 0. They include:
    - `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` ("this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (1 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)");
    - `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main`;
    - `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` (locally it reads no PR body; CI reads this one);
    - `check:nul-bytes`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:skill-examples` and `check:lean-entry-closure`. The client, client-react and objectql dependency closures were built first.
  - NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. It exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`) because it needs every package built, and 33 export entries here have no `dist/` (apps, `cloud-connection` and the connectors among them). Left to CI.

- `check-platform-checklist --changed-from`: not run. No export was renamed or removed; two were added.
- **Not run locally, with the reason:** `test:repo` (no repo-project test changed, and the derivation does not name it) and `pnpm lint` (a repo-wide scan, which CI owns).
- `origin/main` has since moved to `973917c579`. The 6 commits touch no `lint` file and no file this PR edits (one is in `metadata-protocol`'s seed loader). The branch was not re-merged, because there is no conflict.
- **CI check-runs:** this body is written once, at create. The seat reads the PR's check-runs.

## File surface beyond the claim, and why

- `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`: one optional interface member, `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope`. It is the only typed channel from the gate to a rule (G1). No open PR touches the file (17 open PRs' file lists read in this act).
- `packages/lint/src/index.ts`: two exports. `rule-id-barrel-exports.test.ts` went red without the id (1 failed of 6934).
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, one sentence. Its "That changes what a rule can **resolve**, never what it judges" became false for this rule, so it now reads "never which rules run" and names the one rule that is told the closure is in force.

## Acceptance notes

- A write that names no package and binds an object that exists nowhere is still accepted silently at the view door: overlay `nosuch_obj` answers `200` with `advisories: []`, pinned as unchanged here. A flow on the same overlay write gets `flow-trigger-unknown-object`. This PR keeps the overlay door as the dispatch ruled. The reach of this case was measured through `saveMetaItem` over a stub engine, not through a booted HTTP door.
- The two door verdicts for an out-of-closure object reference disagree (P2: flow advisory, dataset refusal). This view follows the flow's.
- `list-view-object-outside-closure` has no `os explain` entry. The CLI never emits it, and the hint carries the remedy.
- The first commit's subject reads `fix(lint)!:`. It was written before G3 was settled and is left as is (no force-push). The PR title is the squash subject.
